description: Example agents.json — single-record template. Copy to <host>:/srv/agents/index.json (live, NOT in repo), edit, restart agent-dashboard.service. Per-agent capabilities and services are derived at runtime from /etc/openclaw/agent-defaults.json (in this same repo, agent-defaults.json) based on role + integrations. This file carries only flags and host-specific data.
_doc_code_root: Host-level operational settings for the shared code tree where coding agents create worktrees, edit projects, and commit. install.sh's drift-check reads these and warns if filesystem state diverges from declared intent. A future `openclaw add-agent` script will read them to know where to bootstrap a new coding agent's workspace + what git identity to wire in.

agents._doc_role: role is exclusive: 'coding' (modifies code, works tickets) OR 'monitor' (triages incidents, wakes/restarts other agents, sends alerts). Never both. Derived capabilities and services come from agent-defaults.json byRole[role].
agents._doc_integrations: Each truthy integration adds services and capabilities via agent-defaults.json byIntegration[k]. Turning an integration off removes both. Available: webhook, gmail, maildir, jira, bitbucket, openaiAuth, claudeAuth, telegram.
agents._doc_overrides: Optional `capabilities` overrides individual keys (e.g. read-only mode: { can_modify_code: false }). Optional `services` adds extras to the derived list. For project-specific add-ons, drop a file in ~/<user>/.config/openclaw/projects/<name>.json (convention — not yet wired into the loader).
